sources.title: Security Incident | Recovery Update #3: 90% of Stolen Assets Replenished; Proof of Reserves Snapshot Provided
claims: Binance states that the covered amount has increased from approximately 80% to 90% of the incident loss.
Binance states that BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC are fully backed at 100% in the new snapshot.
Binance states that the new Proof of Reserves snapshot was taken at 2026-10-31 00:00 UTC and has been updated on its PoR website.
Binance estimates that full zero-knowledge proof generation requires 40 to 50 hours and may be available by 2026-11-03 UTC.
Binance states that the remaining 10% consists of tokens outside the ten named assets and that these assets are less liquid.
Binance states that replenishment uses a partial SAFU deployment, a portion of the Futures Insurance Fund and corporate treasury.
Binance says partial SAFU deployment is expected over the following 24 hours and that SAFU will be replenished to approximately USD 1 billion.
Binance says the remaining Futures Insurance Fund is above its required risk-management level.
Binance targets resuming withdrawals on 2026-11-01, subject to its security process.
limitations: These are Binance's own statements and have not yet been independently reconciled to the complete address-level reserve set and customer-liability dataset.
The full zero-knowledge proof was not yet available at the capture cutoff; Binance estimated availability by 2026-11-03.
The announcement does not disclose XRP units purchased, XRP-specific USD purchases, venue split between spot and OTC, or the exact source of XRP replenishment.
The statement '100% backed' is recorded as a minimum 1:1 coverage claim, not an independently recomputed exact reserve ratio.
The aggregate 90% coverage figure is not converted into a dollar amount because the announcement does not provide a token-by-token reconciliation.
A Proof of Reserves snapshot covers the disclosed custody scope; it is not a complete audit of all liabilities, corporate solvency or operational controls.

sources.title: Security Incident Update #2
claims: Binance previously stated that more than USD 6.34 billion in company funds had been set aside.
Binance stated that approximately USD 5 billion was already held in exact affected token assets at that time.
Binance said it was acquiring remaining affected token assets through market and OTC channels.
limitations: The update predates Recovery Update #3 and is a prior-state company statement.
It does not disclose XRP-specific purchase amounts or execution venues.

sources.title: Proof of Reserves methodology
claims: Binance describes address ownership verification, customer-balance snapshots, zk-SNARK proof generation and Merkle-tree inclusion verification.
The page describes user self-verification of inclusion in the liabilities report.
limitations: The web-rendered page did not expose the newly updated asset-level table in machine-readable text at this capture.
The methodology page is not an independent third-party audit.

sources.title: Binance hack drained wallets backing customer assets, reserve data shows
claims: CoinDesk reports that the Ethereum wallet labelled Binance 14 appeared in Binance's 2026-10-01 Proof of Reserves address set.
CoinDesk reports that Binance 14 held approximately 89,475 ETH and 1.26 billion USDT at the October 1 snapshot.
limitations: This source's wallet example is Ethereum-specific and does not establish that the five XRPL source wallets were in the October 1 XRP reserve set.
Its analysis predates Recovery Update #3 and must not be used as the current October 31 reserve ratio.

sources.title: Binance Estimates $6.3bn Impact From Security Incident, Pledges to Cover All Losses
claims: The report reproduces an October 1, 2026 XRP reserve ratio of 100.77%.
The report gives October 1 XRP customer net account balances of approximately 2.496 billion XRP.
The report gives October 1, 2025 XRP customer net account balances of approximately 2.753 billion XRP.
limitations: The values are historical October 1 figures, not the October 31 post-incident snapshot.
The displayed token quantities are rounded; any implied reserve balance is approximate.
The source reproduces exchange PoR data and is not a separate custody attestation.

sources.title: Crypto exchanges call for quick moves to bolster defenses after Binance heist
claims: Reuters reports that Coinbase said it adjusted systems that store cryptocurrency keys offline as a precaution after the Binance incident.
Reuters reports that exchanges called for faster industry-wide incident information sharing and coordinated response.
limitations: This is a custody/security response, not evidence of a Coinbase XRP-specific product or reserve change.
Reuters does not disclose the exact Coinbase control changes.

sources.title: XRP ETF dashboard
claims: The dashboard reports a USD 8.4 million net inflow on October 29, 2026 across five U.S. spot XRP funds.
The dashboard reports USD 98.9 million net inflow over the preceding 30 sessions and USD 1.73 billion cumulative net inflow since November 14, 2025.
limitations: The dashboard's latest completed session at capture was October 29.
It states that fund net assets and holdings are not published in its flow series; cumulative flow is not current AUM or a current coin-balance measure.
ETF creations/redemptions can settle after the flow report and do not by themselves predict same-day XRP price.

independence_policy.rule: Binance statements are one issuer/exchange source family. CoinDesk, The Edge, Reuters and Alpha Finance are separate publishers but must not be assumed fully independent of underlying exchange data.
independence_policy.corroboration: Treat primary company statements, independent address-level chain reconstruction, reserve-address ownership, customer-liability proofs and third-party market data as distinct evidence classes.
independence_policy.feature_admission: The recovery announcement may enter the event timeline. Do not admit its aggregate coverage percentage or ETF gross/cumulative flow as a directional XRP price feature without point-in-time reconciliation.
